subject.title: Update 2026.3.24 silently drops config when HOME changes

question: When updater HOME differs from the installed gateway service HOME and no explicit OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH or OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR exists, should OpenClaw preserve the service HOME, block and require explicit migration, or add a guarded doctor migration?
rationale: The fix crosses config, credentials, service ownership, and Unix-user trust boundaries, while current code intentionally drops stale service env for security.

options.title: Block and require migration
options.body: Detect the mismatch before config or service rewrite, stop with both roots shown, and route recovery through an explicit doctor migration path.

options.title: Preserve authenticated service HOME
options.body: Carry the installed service HOME only after proving the unit is OpenClaw-owned and belongs to the target service identity.

options.title: Document manual recovery only
options.body: Keep runtime behavior unchanged and rely on runbook guidance for operators who update from the wrong HOME.

recommendation.title: Block and require migration
recommendation.body: Detect the mismatch before config or service rewrite, stop with both roots shown, and route recovery through an explicit doctor migration path.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision centers on update/service-refresh behavior where this history points most strongly to recent area ownership.
